Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-5ED3BAB6CA-81537
Member: Harper Alvarez, Member ID W597643658
Plan: Kentucky Medicaid [Managed Care Organization name — not stated in the denial notice]
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-06
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial dated 2026-08-06 (Reference POC-5ED3BAB6CA-81537) of prior authorization for CPT 63030, lower back disc surgery/decompression, for member Harper Alvarez. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." Based on the documentation in the prior authorization packet, this stated basis for denial is not consistent with the clinical record, and I ask that the determination be reversed.

At the outset, I note that the denial notice does not identify the specific medical policy, clinical guideline, or criteria document that was applied to reach this determination, nor does it name the managed care organization administering this Kentucky Medicaid benefit. I am unable to cite or quote that document because it was not provided. I am requesting, as part of this appeal, that the plan identify in writing the specific policy and criteria relied upon in the original denial, consistent with the plan's obligation to disclose the guidelines used in adverse benefit determinations.

In the absence of a plan-specific document to quote, I have reviewed a publicly available Aetna national Clinical Policy Bulletin, Number 0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion," which sets out criteria commonly applied to this exact procedure (lumbar laminectomy/discectomy for herniated disc). I am not asserting that this specific bulletin is the document the plan applied to Harper's case — that has not been confirmed — but I offer it as an illustration of the type of criteria generally used for this procedure, against which the record here can be measured. That bulletin states, in relevant part:

"Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met... All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out... Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy... and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression."

Mapping the clinical record for Harper Alvarez to each of these elements:

1. Duration and nature of symptoms: Harper has experienced 24 months of progressive lower back pain unrelieved by rest — a chronic, worsening condition, not an acute or self-limited episode.

2. Conservative therapy — physical therapy: Harper completed a supervised course of physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, over 10 weeks (2026-04-24 through 2026-07-03), totaling 16 completed visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This is a structured, supervised, multi-week course of conservative care substantially exceeding the 6-week benchmark referenced above.

3. Conservative therapy — medication: Harper was treated with NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, representing a prolonged pharmacologic trial that failed to control symptoms.

4. Conservative therapy — injection: Harper received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which produced only 4 weeks of partial relief before symptoms recurred, demonstrating that even interventional conservative treatment did not achieve durable improvement.

5. Imaging correlating with clinical findings: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-24 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is graded as severe, and the location corresponds directly to Harper's clinical presentation.

6. Neurologic/functional findings correlating with the imaged level: Harper has radicular pain radiating into the right calf and cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, reflecting a significant limitation in activities of daily living. Physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged L4-L5 level.

7. Absence of contraindications: The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status, none of which raise a barrier to surgical treatment.

Taken together, the record documents 24 months of progressive symptoms; a supervised, multi-modality conservative treatment course spanning physical therapy (10 weeks/16 visits), 8 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection, all with inadequate or only temporary relief; objective imaging showing severe, level-corresponding nerve root compression; and a physical examination and functional history consistent with that imaging. This directly contradicts the stated basis for denial that conservative treatment was not adequately trialed or documented.

I am requesting that the plan:
1. Overturn the denial of CPT 63030 and issue authorization for the requested lumbar decompression/discectomy;
2. If the plan's applicable medical policy differs from the criteria discussed above, provide the specific policy name, number, and the exact criteria used, so that the record can be addressed against the actual standard applied; and
3. Offer a peer-to-peer review between the plan's medical director and Dr. Duval, the treating orthopedic surgeon, to discuss the clinical findings prior to a final appeal determination.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03); documentation of the 8-month NSAID trial; the corticosteroid injection record (2026-04-21); the MRI report dated 2026-06-24; and the surgeon's clinical examination notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the applicable internal appeal deadline and process, as the denial notice states an appeal window of 180 days (by 2027-02-02), which I ask the plan to confirm in writing is accurate for this Kentucky Medicaid plan.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal. Please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address], or Dr. Duval's office at [Provider Office Phone Number], with any questions or to schedule a peer-to-peer review.

Sincerely,

Harper Alvarez
